content.text: Hubble counters are noisy and don't clearly show a network fault. I'll check when route-service's spans stop, and whether its pod or JVM metrics stop or reset.

input.query: SELECT src, substr(CAST(time AS VARCHAR),1,19) minute, COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT 'abn' src,* FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm',* FROM normal_traces) WHERE service_name='ts-route-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT src, substr(CAST(time AS VARCHAR),1,16) mn, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, MAX(attr_k8s_pod_name) pod FROM (SELECT 'abn' src,* FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm',* FROM normal_traces) WHERE service_name='ts-route-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Route-service emitted its last spans at about 09:52 and nothing after, under the same pod name, while its memory reset. Before settling on that, I'll compare server-span latency and error counts across all services to check for other faults.

input.query: SELECT service_name, src, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95ms, SUM(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, COUNT(DISTINCT span_name) nspan FROM (SELECT 'abn' src,* FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm',* FROM normal_traces) WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Most other services are quiet in the abnormal window, which is consistent with a route-service outage starving its callers of traffic. I'll check the pod uptime and restart counters for route-service directly.

input.query: SELECT 'sum' t, metric, COUNT(*) n, MIN(value) mn, MAX(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'k8s.%' AND (metric LIKE '%restart%' OR metric LIKE '%uptime%') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'gauge', metric, COUNT(*), MIN(value), MAX(value) FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric LIKE '%restart%' OR metric LIKE '%uptime%' GROUP BY ALL

SELECT service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, MIN(value) mn, MAX(value) mx, COUNT(*) n, MIN(CAST(time AS VARCHAR)) t0, MAX(CAST(time AS VARCHAR)) t1 FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' GROUP BY ALL HAVING MAX(value)>0 OR MIN(value)>0 ORDER BY mx DESC

content.text: Two pods show restart counters: route-service at 1 and ts-ticket-office-service at 3, both flat across the window. I need the normal-period baseline to tell whether these restarts are new.

input.query: SELECT service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, MIN(value) mn, MAX(value) mx, COUNT(*) n, MIN(CAST(time AS VARCHAR)) t0, MAX(CAST(time AS VARCHAR)) t1 FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' GROUP BY ALL HAVING MAX(value)>0 ORDER BY mx DESC

SELECT 'metric' src, service_name, COUNT(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-ticket-office%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'trace', service_name, COUNT(*) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-ticket%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'log', service_name, COUNT(*) FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name LIKE '%ticket%' OR attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'ts-ticket%' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: Ticket-office's restart count of 3 is baseline (it is also present in normal), so it is not a fault. Route-service's restart counter went from 0 in normal to 1 in the abnormal window, and its spans stopped at the same moment. I have enough to conclude.

input.reflection: Findings: ts-ui-dashboard /api/v1/routeservice/routes returns 503 after ~3.5s (118 errors), with no child spans. ts-route-service restart counter went 0 (normal) -> 1 (abnormal) at ~09:52:36, memory working set fell from ~840MB to ~1.6MB, and its server spans stop after 09:52 for the rest of the window (4 spans vs 1482 normal). ts-ticket-office restarts=3 is baseline in normal too, so ignore. Other services' drop in traffic is consistent with downstream starvation of route-service callers (basic, route-plan, travel). Only error-bearing service is ui-dashboard. Conclusion: root cause ts-route-service, kind pod_unavailable (restarted and never resumed serving in window). Propagation: ts-route-service -> ts-ui-dashboard (user-facing).
